query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A physics-informed machine learning (ML) model that explicitly incorporates lattice‐distortion scattering parameters (mass‐fluctuation and strain‐field descriptors) together with ab initio–derived elastic and vibrational features will identify equimolar high‐entropy alloys (HEAs) with anomalously low phonon thermal conductivity (κ_ph) more accurately than current empirical‐descriptor models.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar, single‐phase, 4–5‐component FCC or BCC high‐entropy alloys prepared by arc melting and homogenized to eliminate ordering or secondary phases.
generation.intervention: Application of a hybrid ML model trained on (i) mass‐ and strain‐field fluctuation descriptors derived from the alloy composition and (ii) DFT‐computed elastic/vibrational features, to predict κ_ph.
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 300–800 K; microstructure: equiaxed, grain size >5 µm; no significant phase separation or ordering.
generation.structural_mediator: Lattice distortion–induced phonon scattering quantified via mass‐fluctuation and strain‐field variance parameters.
generation.mechanism: By embedding physical scattering metrics in the feature set, the ML model more accurately captures reductions in phonon mean free path due to multi‐element disorder, yielding lower prediction error.
generation.predicted_outcome: For a test set of equimolar HEAs, the physics‐informed ML model will achieve a mean absolute error (MAE) on κ_ph predictions of ≤0.7 W/m·K, representing ≥30% improvement over a leading empirical‐descriptor baseline (MAE ≈1.0 W/m·K).
generation.baseline: Current empirical‐descriptor ML models predict κ_ph with MAE ≈1.0 W/m·K under the same conditions.
generation.boundary: Valid for equimolar 4–5‐component FCC or BCC HEAs without ordering or secondary phases and measured between 300–800 K; may not generalize to non‐equimolar or multi‐phase alloys.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; generalization to non‐equimolar or ordered HEAs and high‐temperature anharmonic effects beyond 800 K remain untested.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize ten equimolar HEAs predicted by the physics‐informed ML model to have the lowest κ_ph. Measure κ_ph for each alloy from 300 to 800 K using the 3ω method. In parallel, predict κ_ph for these same alloys using the baseline empirical‐descriptor ML model.
measurements: Predicted κ_ph for each alloy by both models
Absolute prediction errors for both models
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if (a) more than 2 of the 10 measured κ_ph values deviate from the physics‐informed model predictions by >15%, or (b) the baseline empirical‐descriptor model attains an MAE ≤0.7 W/m·K on the same test set.
